turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll systematically analyze the training data to identify the key device physics principles driving high PCE, then apply them to the candidate pool.

## Step 1: Extract Patterns from Training Data

### Composition trends (top performers >20%):
- **FAMAPbBrI** dominates the highest efficiencies (19–22.9%)
- **CsFAMAPbBrI** also very strong (17–20.6%)
- **FAMAPbI** competitive (14–20.4%)
- **FAPbI** solid (15–20.2%)
- Mixed Pb halide perovskites with FA+MA cations consistently outperform single-cation systems

### Architecture:
- Both nip and pin appear at the top; nip slightly more represented at >19%
- pin with PTAA/NiO-c HTL + C60/BCP ETL also reaches 18–20%

### ETL patterns (nip):
- **SnO2-np** or **SnO2-c** (compact) are the best ETLs — better band alignment with FA/MA perovskites, lower trap density than TiO2, no UV degradation
- TiO2-c | TiO2-mp still works well but SnO2 is superior
- Bilayer ETLs (SnO2-c | SnO2-np, SnO2-c | C9, SnO2-np | ImAcHcl) push PCE to 20–20.5%

### HTL patterns (nip):
- **Spiro-MeOTAD** is the dominant high-performance HTL
- PTAA also excellent
- Specialty HTLs (CH3O-PEIA | Spiro-MeOTAD, OAI | DM, SrCl2 | Spiro-MeOTAD) give the very highest values

### Back contact (nip):
- **Au** is the gold standard for nip — better work function match to Spiro-MeOTAD (~5.1 eV)
- Ag works but slightly lower
- MoO3 | Ag interlayer helps

### Deposition:
- **Spin-coating >> Spin-coating** (two-step) or single spin-coating both work
- Anti-solvent/gas reaction steps help crystallinity

### pin architecture top performers:
- ETL: C60 | BCP or PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP
- HTL: PTAA or NiO-c | PTAA
- Back contact: Cu or Ag
- Composition: CsFAMAPbBrI or FAMAPbBrI

## Step 2: Score Each Candidate

Let me focus on the most promising candidates:

**c047** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Excellent composition (top performer class)
- SnO2-c ETL (proven high performer — analogous to FAMAPbBrI/SnO2-c/Spiro/Au = 16.45–17.88% in training)
- Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: ideal HTL/contact pair
- Single spin-coating; comparable entries: 16.45–17.88%
- **Estimated: ~17–18%**

**c008** — FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- FAMAPbI with SnO2-c ETL, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, two-step spin
- Training analog: FAMAPbI/nip/ITO/SnO2-c/Spiro/Ag = 18.5%; with Au instead of Ag should be ≥18.5%
- Two-step deposition improves film quality
- **Estimated: ~18.5–19%**

**c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN-Br, Cu
- CsFAMAPbBrI pin with C60|BCP ETL, PTAA|PFN-Br HTL, Cu contact
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/pin/ITO/C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu = 18.15–18.35%
- PFN-Br interlayer improves hole extraction and reduces interface recombination
- Cu back contact: excellent work function match (~5.0 eV) to PTAA
- **Estimated: ~18.5–19.5%**

**c089** — FAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60, PTAA, Ag
- FAMAPbBrI pin with C60 ETL (no BCP), PTAA HTL, Ag
- Training analog: FAMAPbBrI/pin/DWCNTs/C60|BCP/PTAA|PFN-P2/Cu = 15.6%; FAPbI/pin/ITO/C60/PTAA/Ag = 10.76%
- Without BCP buffer, electron extraction less selective; PTAA is excellent HTL
- **Estimated: ~15–17%**

**c093** — CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|FTO, PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA, Ag
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/pin/FTO/C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu = 20.1%; with PCBM-60|BCP and Ag instead
- PCBM-60|BCP is slightly less optimal than C60|BCP for pin (C60 has better electron mobility), but PTAA is excellent
- FTO substrate slightly rougher than ITO but workable
- **Estimated: ~18–20%**

**c036** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, NDI;SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- NDI (naphthalene diimide) + SnO2-np bilayer ETL — NDI is an n-type organic with good electron transport, SnO2-np provides good coverage
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/nip/FTO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Au = 17.795%
- NDI additive may improve ETL/perovskite interface
- **Estimated: ~17–18%**

**c059** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-QDs, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- SnO2 quantum dots as ETL — high surface area, good band alignment, proven in literature
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/nip/FTO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Au = 17.795%; SnO2-QDs may be comparable or slightly better
- **Estimated: ~17.5–18.5%**

**c061** — CsFAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|C60-SAM, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- CsFAPbI with SnO2-c + C60-SAM bilayer ETL — C60-SAM provides excellent passivation of ETL/perovskite interface, reduces recombination
- Training analog: CsFAPbI/nip/FTO/SnO2-c/Spiro/Au = 15.71%; C60-SAM interlayer should push higher
- **Estimated: ~17–19%**

**c079** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-np, CsPbBr3-np|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- SnO2-np ETL (excellent), CsPbBr3-np as HTL interlayer before Spiro — QD interlayer can improve band alignment and reduce recombination at HTL interface
- Training analog: FAMAPbBrI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Au = 19.13–19.5%
- CsPbBr3-np interlayer is a known passivation strategy
- **Estimated: ~19–20%**

**c092** — FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag
- FAMAPbI with SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag
- Training analog: FAMAPbI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Ag = 19.5%; MoO3 interlayer improves hole injection from Ag
- **Estimated: ~19–20%**

**c062** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|PCBM-60, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Au
- Bilayer ETL (SnO2-np + PCBM-60), Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Au
- PCBM-60 on top of SnO2-np provides additional passivation and electron selectivity
- MoO3|Au back contact: MoO3 improves hole extraction, Au is ideal
- Training analog: FAMAPbBrI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Au = 19.13–19.5%; bilayer ETL + MoO3 should push higher
- **Estimated: ~19.5–21%**

**c015** — CsFAMAPbBrI|(EPA)PbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- Passivated CsFAMAPbBrI with EPA surface treatment, standard TiO2 bilayer ETL
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI|(oFPEA)PbI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro/Au = 19.695%
- But uses TiO2 (not SnO2) and FTO — slightly lower ceiling
- **Estimated: ~16–18%**

**c049** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Carbozole@S12, Au
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/nip/FTO/TiO2-c|TiO2-mp/Carbozole@S14/Au = 14.365%
- S12 vs S14 carbazole HTL — similar class, S14 gave 14.365%; S12 likely comparable
- **Estimated: ~13–15%**

**c034** — CsFAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbI/nip/FTO/TiO2-c|TiO2-mp/Spiro/Au = 18.66%; ITO substrate, two-step
- **Estimated: ~18–19%**

**c038** — CsFAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au
- Triple ETL stack: TiO2-c | TiO2-mp | SnO2-c — mesoporous TiO2 scaffold + SnO2 capping layer
- Training analog: CsFAMAPbBrI/nip/FTO/TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|SnO2/Spiro/Au = 19.16%
- CsFAPbI composition slightly lower ceiling than CsFAMAPbBrI
- **Estimated: ~17–19%**

## Step 3: Final Ranking of Top Candidates

Ranking by estimated PCE:

1. **c062** — FAMAPbBrI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np|PCBM-60/Spiro/MoO3|Au — best composition + bilayer ETL with PCBM-60 passivation + MoO3|Au contact (~20–21%)

2. **c079** — FAMAPbBrI/nip/FTO/SnO2-np/CsPbBr3-np|Spiro/Au — top composition + SnO2-np + QD interlayer at HTL interface (~19.5–20%)

3. **c092** — FAMAPbI/nip/ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro/MoO3|Ag — strong composition + SnO2-np + MoO3 interlayer (~19–20%)

4. **c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI/pin/ITO/C60|BCP/PTAA|PFN-Br/Cu — excellent pin stack with PFN-Br passivation (~18.5–19.5%)

5. **c008** — FAMAPbI/nip/ITO/SnO2-c/Spiro/Au/two-step — proven high-performance stack with two-step deposition (~18.5–19%)

Close runners-up: c093, c047, c061, c034, c059

---

**Final: c062, c079, c092, c085, c008**
